title: Geometric and Zariski immediate specializations on universally catenary schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is universally catenary: for every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, every finite-type $A$-algebra is catenary in the bounded saturated-chain sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $y\ne x$ be points of $X$ with $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$. The following conditions are equivalent. (1) There is no point strictly between $y$ and $x$ in the specialization order; equivalently the local ring of the reduced closure $\overline{\{y\}}$ at $x$ has Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. (2) There exists a geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ above $y\rightsquigarrow x$ for which the reduced closure of the image of $\bar y$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$ has dimension one [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. In particular, every immediate geometric specialization projects to a saturated inclusion of the corresponding primes on any affine neighbourhood of $x$. No regularity, field of definition, or coefficient sheaf is assumed.

source.place: Expose XIV, Definitions 2.1.1–2.1.2 and Proposition 2.1.4, printed pp.209–211.

proof.text: Put $Z=\overline{\{y\}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{Z,x}$. Choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $x$; it also contains every generalization of $x$, hence $y$. Write $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ for their primes. Then $R=(A/\mathfrak p)_{\mathfrak q/\mathfrak p}$, a nonfield local domain. Its primes correspond to primes of $A$ between $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$. Thus there is no point strictly between $y$ and $x$ exactly when $R$ has only its zero and maximal primes. By the prime-chain definition of [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], this is equivalent to $\dim R=1$: an intermediate prime gives a chain of length two; if there is none, the zero-to-maximal chain has length one and every chain has length at most one.

source.place: Expose XIV, Definitions 2.1.1–2.1.2 and Proposition 2.1.4, printed pp.209–211.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion] to the given $X,x,y$. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is Noetherian, $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$, and universal catenarity on every affine open implies its affine-cover hypothesis. Its concluding equivalence states that $y\rightsquigarrow x$ is an immediate geometric specialization, meaning codimension one in a strict localization at a geometric point above $x$, if and only if $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,x}=1$; it also states independence of that geometric point. This is precisely condition (2) equivalent to the dimension-one clause of condition (1). The cited statement already includes existence of the immediate specialization; no inference from a possibly empty set of lifts is being made. Together with Step 1 it proves the equivalence of (1) and (2).

source.place: Expose XIV, Definitions 2.1.1–2.1.2 and Proposition 2.1.4, printed pp.209–211.

proof.text: For any specified immediate geometric specialization, its image in $X_{(\bar x)}$ lies over $y$ and has one-dimensional closure. Part (b) of [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion] therefore gives $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,x}=1$. The argument of Step 1 applies on any affine neighbourhood of $x$ and excludes every prime strictly between $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$, so the prime inclusion is saturated there. Universal catenarity is used only in the cited converse, and no regularity, field of definition, or coefficient assumption has entered.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NJ-a1b2310a8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the report, the existing node it cites (lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion), def-per-potential-dualizing, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, the strict-henselization and geometric-point definitions, and ILO XIV §2.1 (Def. 2.1.1–2.1.2, Prop. 2.1.3–2.1.4 and Lemmas 2.1.5–2.1.6 with proofs, printed pp. 209–211). Shape: one commit, the item plus the report, no new nodes. The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; there is no SGA citation. Both this item and the criterion are still unsplit live, so the delivery is not superseded. The item's (1)⇔(2) is ILO 2.1.4 with the x/y convention swapped, and the item's universal catenarity (on every affine open) implies the criterion's affine-cover hypothesis. Step 1 is elementary and correct: O_{Z,x}=(A/p)_{q/p}, its primes are those between p and q, and every intermediate point lies in the affine chart. Step 2 cites the criterion's final clause, which defines immediate through def-per-potential-dualizing, so it includes existence. I checked (a) myself: points over y are minimal primes of the flat strict henselization O^sh_{Z,x}, so their closures have dimension exactly 1, and the fibre over y is nonempty by faithful flatness. Step 3 applies (b) and then Step 1, which gives saturation. Edge cases: a field; a DVR; A² localized at the origin with y the generic point (both sides false); A² with y the generic point of the line {t=0} and x the origin (both sides true; this is the case that broke the X_(x̄)-component node returned in Q05). The criterion is in the same unit, has no proof, and Q05's split of it never cited this item, so there is no cycle and no tool_uses are needed. Citing an existing restatement is allowed by brief §2.
